plan.analysis: The seed is the constant function giving R=2/3. Known analytic shapes suggest a Gaussian gives 1/√2≈0.707, so non-constant shapes can improve. We will spend the round on two independent gradient-based optimizations of the heights: one initialized with a Gaussian, one with a flexible parametric family (flat-top/parabola) followed by gradient refinement. This explores both local optimization from a good guess and a structured family. We expect at least one to exceed 0.70 and give a strong new state to build on. Thread T1 tracks the search for better shapes.

theory.statement: A symmetric, unimodal shape (Gaussian-like or flat-top) will yield a higher R than the constant function because it makes the autoconvolution flatter in the center.
theory.refuted_if: Gradient ascent from such shapes fails to exceed 2/3 by a margin.
theory.why: Analytic calculation for a Gaussian gives R=1/√2≈0.707; a flat-top may be better.

threads.question: Find a non-constant shape with R > 2/3, and push it as high as possible.
threads.stop: When the record has not improved by 0.0003 over the last 3 actions spanning at least 2 rounds.

actions.hypothesis: Gaussian-initialized gradient ascent will beat 0.6667 and reach >0.70.
actions.change: Implement a new construct: set N=200. Initialize h as a Gaussian centered at N/2 with std=0.15*N, normalized. Then run a gradient ascent loop: while time.process_time() < budget_seconds - margin, compute numerical gradient of R(h) via central finite differences, update h += lr * grad, project h = max(h,0), renormalize to sum 1. Adapt lr (halve if R decreases, double if increases). Keep best h. If stalled, restart from a trapezoid (flat top 0.2*N, linear taper to 0.4*N). Return best h.

actions.hypothesis: Optimizing a parametric family then refining with gradient ascent will also exceed 0.70 and may find a different local optimum.
actions.change: Implement a new construct: set N=200. First maximize R over p,q for the shape h[i] = (1 - |2*i/N - 1|^p)^q using scipy.optimize.minimize (Nelder-Mead) with p,q>0. Start with p=2,q=1. Then, using the best p,q, generate h as the initial guess for the same gradient ascent loop as in the first experiment (numerical gradient, projection, adaptive lr). Run until budget is nearly exhausted. Return best h.
actions.prediction: R will exceed 0.70, possibly comparable to or better than the Gaussian initialization.

plan.analysis: p0002 reached 0.810 with a slow finite-difference gradient (only ~4300 iterations in 85 s). Its bottleneck is optimizer cost, not the shape idea; the asymmetric peaked profile is clearly better than the flat-top (0.724). I will spend this round on two well-funded fast-gradient experiments built on p0002: one multi-resolution exact-gradient refinement (the main expected win), and one heavy random-restart/asymmetric-seed search using the same fast gradient to test whether a different basin beats 0.810. T1 is not due; T2 is opened for the discretization/optimizer question.

theory.statement: The main limitation of p0002 is its O(N) finite-difference gradient: an exact/adjoint gradient makes each iteration O(N log N), so many more iterations and much larger N become affordable, which should raise R well above 0.810.
theory.refuted_if: An exact-gradient L-BFGS refinement at N=200, then upsampled to N>=1000, fails to improve p0002 by at least 0.005.
theory.why: p0002 used 81 s for about 4300 iterations, most of the time spent on finite differences; the shape is still improving when time ran out.

threads.question: Does exact-gradient optimization at higher discretization N (200 -> 1000+) improve R beyond the N=200 finite-difference result?
threads.stop: When multi-resolution exact-gradient refinement has not raised the record by 0.0003 over 3 actions spanning at least 2 rounds.

actions.hypothesis: Exact-gradient L-BFGS-B from p0002, followed by coarse-to-fine upsampling, reaches R > 0.83.
actions.change: Implement construct on the p0002 state. Write an exact R_score and its gradient: with L = convolve(h,h) padded by zeros, let G_k = (2L_k + L_{k-1} + L_{k+1})/3, then dL2/dh_i = sum_k G_k h_{k-i} (compute by convolution/correlation). l1=(sum h)^2 so dl1/dh_i=2*sum(h). linf uses only the active maximum knot m, so dlinf/dh_i = h_{m-i} with zero if m-i out of range. Combine dR via quotient rule. Use scipy.optimize.minimize(method='L-BFGS-B', jac=True, bounds=[(0,None)]*N). Start from start if given else from the p0002 construction brought by the harness. First run at N = len(start) (or 200) with many iterations; then repeatedly upsample best h by a factor 2 (np.interp or linear interpolation), renormalize, and re-run L-BFGS-B, up to N <= 4000 or until time nearly exhausted. Keep the best by exact R_score and use the full budget.
actions.prediction: R reaches at least 0.83, and the shape remains asymmetric with f*f maximum near 0.70 of support.

actions.hypothesis: Fast exact-gradient ascent from several strongly perturbed/asymmetric seeds finds a better basin than p0002, giving R > 0.81.
actions.change: Implement the same exact-gradient L-BFGS-B optimizer as in the other experiment, but use it for multi-start exploration rather than multi-resolution. Generate seeds: (a) p0002 with large smooth multiplicative perturbations, (b) asymmetric lognormal/gamma-like profiles shifted and skewed within the support, (c) mixtures of two or three Gaussians with random centers/widths, (d) heavily resampled/blocky asymmetric profiles. Normalize each, run exact-gradient L-BFGS-B for a limited number of iterations, keep the best. Use any remaining time to refine the global best at higher N (upsample and re-optimize). Keep and return the best construction found.
actions.prediction: Either a new basin beats 0.810 or the run confirms p0002 is a strong local optimum; in both cases it gives useful evidence about the shape class.

plan.analysis: p0005's big gain confirms a sparse, strongly asymmetric basin: 65% zeros, max/mean 6.33, autocorrelation peak at 0.09 of support. The smooth centred p0004 basin is much weaker (0.816). The remaining opportunity is to push the boundary-concentrated basin further and test whether even more extreme left-edge concentration yields a better basin. I will spend 3 units on a careful high-resolution refinement of p0005 (exact gradient, upsampling with reoptimization and local perturbations), 2 units on multi-start from extreme left-concentrated seeds, and 1 mutation around p0005 for cheap local variation.

theory.statement: R is maximized by shapes whose mass is concentrated near one edge, making the autoconvolution peak near the boundary and sparse; p0005 is an example, and even more extreme left-edge concentration may yield higher R.
theory.refuted_if: Multi-start from strongly left-concentrated seeds and high-resolution refinement of p0005 fail to exceed 0.833241 by a meaningful margin.
theory.why: p0005 (0.833) beats the smooth centred p0004 (0.816), and its f*f peak is at 0.09 of support.

theory.statement: Exact analytic gradients plus L-BFGS-B make high-N refinement cheap, but gains depend on re-optimizing after each upsampling step and preserving the sparse/asymmetric structure.
theory.why: p0005 shows exact gradients enable multi-start exploration; p0004 shows naive upsampling gives only modest gains.

threads.question: Does concentrating f toward one edge (sparse support, f*f peak near the boundary) raise R beyond 0.833, and can extreme left-concentrated seeds find a better basin?
threads.stop: When three actions on extreme-asymmetric seeds/refinement have not raised the record by 0.0003 over at least two rounds.

actions.hypothesis: High-resolution exact-gradient refinement of p0005, with reoptimization after every upsampling and small local perturbations, will push the sparse boundary-concentrated basin above 0.833241.
actions.change: Start from the p0005 construction. Implement exact analytic R and its gradient; run scipy L-BFGS-B with jac=True and bounds [(0,None)] at N=400 for many iterations. Then repeatedly: upsample best h by factor 2 via linear interpolation, renormalize, reoptimize with L-BFGS-B at the new N (up to N=6400), and also try brief local perturbations (smooth multiplicative noise scale 0.02-0.1, preserve sparsity) followed by reoptimization, keeping the best by exact score. Use the full budget and return the best h.
actions.prediction: Reaches at least 0.835; if not, it reports the refined p0005 basin as a strong local optimum.

actions.hypothesis: Seeds concentrated near the left edge, more extreme than p0005, will find an even better basin for R.
actions.change: Generate multi-start seeds concentrated near the left edge: (1-x)^p for p in [0.5,8]; exp(-a x) for a in [1,50]; shifted lognormal/gamma distributions with mode below 0.1 of the support; blocky profiles supported only on a prefix; and p0005 with its nonzero region compressed toward the left. Normalize each, run exact-gradient L-BFGS-B at N=200 or 400 for many iterations, keep the best by exact score, then refine the winner at N up to 1600 if time allows. Return the best construction.
actions.prediction: Either finds a new basin above 0.833241 or confirms p0005 is a strong local optimum in this class.

plan.analysis: Last round: p0006 gained +0.0189 from exact-gradient perturbations at fixed N=400; its long upsample ladder to N=6400 gave nothing. p0008 reached 0.8399 with extreme left concentration, below p0006. I now believe p0006 is a strong local optimum at N=400, and raw upsampling or more extreme edge concentration is not the path. This round I fund a heavier structural perturbation search on p0006 (3 units), apply the same exact-gradient perturbation method to the alternate p0008 basin (2 units), and add one mutation around p0006 (1 unit). T1 is not due; T2/T3 are not due. I update the theory: drop the extreme-edge H3, revise H2, add H4.

theory.why: F7 shows extreme left-edge concentration gives only 0.8399, below the moderate-spike p0006 basin at 0.8522.

theory.statement: Exact analytic gradients plus L-BFGS-B make refinement cheap, but measured gains come mainly from repeated perturb-and-reoptimize at fixed N=400; raw upsampling to N>=800 without new perturbations did not help.
theory.why: p0006's upsample ladder left R unchanged at 0.833347, while its subsequent N=400 perturbations raised it to 0.852173.

theory.statement: The p0006 basin is a strong local optimum at N=400; more aggressive structural perturbations at N=400, or applying the exact-gradient perturbation method to the alternate p0008 basin, may yield further gains, while raw upsampling and more extreme edge concentration do not.
theory.refuted_if: Aggressive basin-hopping at N=400 and exact-gradient refinement of p0008 both fail to exceed 0.8522.
theory.why: p0006's best gains came from perturbations, but its final many perturbations all returned 0.852173; the alternate p0008 basin has not yet been tried with the exact gradient.

actions.hypothesis: p0006 is near a local optimum at N=400; heavier structural perturbations of its nonzero support followed by exact-gradient L-BFGS will escape to a better basin.
actions.change: Implement exact analytic R and gradient as in p0006. Start from p0006 at N=400. Loop until deadline: copy best_h, apply 1-3 random structural perturbations (scale random contiguous nonzero blocks by factors 0.3-2.5, zero a random block of width up to 10% N, or add a narrow Gaussian spike of height 0.5-3x max at a random position), renormalize; run L-BFGS-B with jac=True, bounds [(0,None)], maxiter 1000; keep best exact score. Every 5th iteration also upsample current best to N=800, perturb, optimize, and if it improves keep it as the new best; else continue at N=400. Return best.
actions.prediction: If p0006 is a strong local optimum, stays near 0.852; if a better nearby basin exists, exceeds 0.853.

actions.hypothesis: The p0008 extreme-edge basin was only refined with finite-difference gradients; applying p0006's exact-gradient perturbation method to it may push it above 0.8522.
actions.change: Implement exact analytic R and gradient as in p0006. Start from p0008 at N=400. Run L-BFGS-B jac=True at N=400 with maxiter 1000. Then repeatedly perturb the current best (multiplicative noise scale 0.02-0.15 on nonzero entries, plus occasional block scaling or zeroing), renormalize, reoptimize, and keep the best exact score. Use the full budget. Return the best construction.
actions.prediction: Either p0008 improves substantially and possibly surpasses 0.8522, or it confirms the extreme-edge basin is inferior.
